report:
Conclusion: The claim is accurate for the U.S. Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) 19.5 mg is FDA-approved and labeled “to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years.” FDA’s approval history lists September 19, 2016, with the indication “for Prevention of Pregnancy for up to Five Years,” and the current prescribing information repeats the same indication. The FDA label identifies the product as containing 19.5 mg levonorgestrel. Bayer’s official HCP site likewise states Kyleena 19.5 mg “is indicated for the prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years,” after which it should be removed/replaced if continued contraception is desired. So the statement correctly reflects the approved duration; it should not be read as a guarantee of effectiveness beyond five years or as approval for other uses.
